evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fonix's Final Results are always pre-announced by a July trading update, and both observed Final Results in the baseline's observed_rns history moved slightly DOWN: -0.63% on 2024-09-24 and -1.83% on 2025-09-23. Applied to this event type the proxy is roughly 4x too large.
evidence.why_not_priced: The FACT is fully priced — that is the finding. What is not priced is the event's own size: with two analysts and no option chain there is no implied move, and any ranker using the baseline's 5.27% proxy will size this print as if it could travel as far as a January trading update. If the market genuinely expected a 5% move into an audit confirmation you would see it in the tape — you would not see a stock sitting in a 167.5-177.0p band for a month on 60-120k shares a day. Instead the pre-print session printed 203,444 shares, still only ~GBP 350k of turnover, which is a thin de-risking, not an event being positioned for.
evidence.independence: Kalkine, 12 August 2026, independently records the price reaction to the same update: the shares fell despite the beat and were 'close to the lower end of a 52-week range spanning roughly 143p to 244p' — https://kalkine.co.uk/news/technology/fonix-dips-as-investors-digest-a-full-year-trading-update-that-beat-expectations. evidence.text: The one number that sets both the dividend and the P/E — adjusted EPS — is the number the market has NOT seen, and it is where the growth is leaking away: H1 FY26 adjusted EPS was exactly FLAT at 6.2p while gross profit rose 7.1% and adjusted EBITDA rose 6.4%, because adjusted PBT grew only 2.6% on rising amortisation of capitalised software (carrying value GBP 2.2m vs GBP 1.8m) and 'a modest rise in the effective corporation tax rate'. The 23 July update disclosed gross profit, adjusted EBITDA and TPV and gave no EPS figure at all.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last time Fonix put a flat adjusted EPS in front of the market was the 17 March 2026 interims (6.2p vs 6.2p) and the stock moved +1.94% — i.e. it was looked through, because the interims also carried a +6.9% interim dividend and an upgraded international narrative. The comparable disappointment is 18 March 2025, -5.21%, the one interim where the delivery did not match the framing. So this line has been both looked through and punished within twelve months; the band is deliberately wide.
evidence.why_not_priced: Adjusted EPS is the denominator of the dividend policy ('at least 75% of adjusted earnings per share') and of the 14.1x forward P/E the screens carry, and it is the only headline Fonix has never pre-announced. FY25 adjusted EPS was 11.3p (FY24 10.8p, +4.6%) and the house broker's FY26 number is 11.5p — +1.8% against adjusted EBITDA up 11.0%. If that gap were in the price you would not see a stock screened on a forward P/E and a 5.63% forecast yield with a 293p consensus target against a 171p close; you would see the target cut. With one house broker publishing (the company's own AIM Rule 26 page lists Cavendish as the only analyst), there is no second estimate to arbitrage the gap.
evidence.independence: The FY25 Annual Report gives the same mechanism a year earlier and the arithmetic to check it against: adjusted EPS 11.3p, adjusted ROCE, underlying cash down 12.4% to GBP 9,877k from GBP 11,324k, and a stated payout of '78% of adjusted EPS as an ordinary dividend' plus a 3p special so that 'total dividends for the year amount to more than 100% of adjusted EPS' — https://www.fonix.com/?jet_download=fe2e3c21121d1ba8d566afde207739f4259b899e (17 Oct 2025). Stockopedia independently carries the 14.14x forward P/E, 5.63% forecast yield and 293p target — https://www.stockopedia.com/share-prices/fonix-LON:FNX/.

evidence.text: Fonix's ability to buy back stock is structurally capped by Rule 9 of the Takeover Code and almost nobody outside the RNS knows it: the concert party holds 33.05% of the share capital, so the company 'has historically been restricted in its ability to conduct share buyback programmes', and the GBP 2.0m 'buyback' every aggregator reported as completed was in fact a SINGLE purchase of exactly 1,250,000 shares (1.25% of capital) at a fixed 159p, only possible because Richard Thompson, through Starnevesse Limited, signed an irrevocable undertaking to sell alongside so the concert party's interest did not increase — his holding fell 7.362603% to 6.149129% in the matching TR-1.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Capital return is the line that moves this stock most. The single largest observed reaction in the baseline's history is 2025-01-23, +5.83%, headlined 'Trading Update and Special Dividend Declaration' — the trading update alone a year later (2026-01-22, no special) moved +5.33%, and 2024-01-24 'Trading Update' moved +9.30%, so the specials are not the whole of it, but this is demonstrably a shareholder-return-owned register. FY26 broke the pattern: no special dividend was declared in January 2026 for the first time, and a GBP 2.0m structured buyback in May replaced it — on 22 May 2026 the shares closed at 159p, the buyback price, and did not re-rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: The structure is only in the RNS PDF. TipRanks describes it as 'completed a GBP 2.0 million share buyback, reflecting strong cash generation and the board's confidence' (https://www.tipranks.com/news/company-announcements/fonix-lifts-profits-and-steps-up-european-push-as-mobile-payments-pipeline-grows) and Kalkine as a 'GBP 2.0 million programme' — neither mentions Rule 9, the 33.05% concert party or the matching irrevocable, and the issuer's own 23 July summary of it says only 'the Group also completed a GBP 2.0m on-market share buyback, underlining the Board's confidence'. So the read available to anyone who did not open the May RNS is 'this company now runs buybacks', when the true read is 'this company can only run a buyback when a named 6.1% holder agrees to sell into it'. If the market knew, the finals' capital-return line would not carry an open-ended-buyback option in the price at all. The direction is modestly negative because it removes an upside scenario rather than creating a downside one: the promised increase in the FINAL DIVIDEND is the one return that needs nobody's permission, and it is contractually ~75-78% of an adjusted EPS that grew ~2% in H1.
evidence.independence: The matching TR-1, a different document filed the same day by a different party: Starnevesse Limited, threshold crossed 22-May-2026, resulting 6.149129% / 6,003,005 shares against a previous notification of 7.362603% — https://www.fonix.com/?jet_download=3d9ff2739423f0be1229997702baa61f25dca27a. The Investegate RNS index corroborates both the 'On Market Share Buyback Programme' row (22 May 2026 07:00) and the 'Transaction in Own Shares and Total Voting Rights' row the same afternoon (22 May 2026 16:46) — a one-day event, not a programme — https://www.investegate.co.uk/company/FNX.

Macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis until the company or a direct counterparty has said it, and this one is not established.

evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Australia has been the line that moves this stock. The 18 Sep 2025 interims, which carried the Australian restructure and the closure of the Bohemia media unit, produced -12.24% -- by far the largest of the 13 observed reactions (median |move| 1.98%). The 24 Nov 2025 trading update, which downgraded the FY25 decline to 7%, produced -5.16%. So this line has moved the stock hard in both directions, and the sign has tracked whether Australia was presented as a continuing problem or as a problem being removed. evidence.why_not_priced: The Investegate RNS record for M&C Saatchi from 1 July 2026 to 21 September 2026 contains nothing but Transaction in Own Shares, three Holding(s) in Company and the Notice of Half Year Results -- no announcement of the MBO, none of its collapse, none of the closure. Sharecast covered this issuer's March 2026 CEO change, so it follows the name, and it did not carry this. If the market had priced the closure of an entire country's advertising operations announced with no consideration and all staff departing, the stock would not be sitting at 147p on 21 September, within 2% of its 52-week high of 150p and up 29% from its April low of 113.5p; nor would a break-up activist have crossed 9% on 18 September. With consensus DPS at nil for both FY26 and FY27 and the Board on record at the FY25 results that it 'believes that greater value can be created for shareholders by increasing the share buyback programme rather than through the payment of a dividend', the interim statement is the natural venue for a replacement programme -- and if none comes, the stock's only mechanical bid has just been withdrawn into a print carrying a closure charge.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 20 Apr 2026 FY results, which announced the reallocation of the final dividend into an enlarged buyback, produced +3.91% -- the best results-day reaction in the 13-event observed record. The 9 March 2026 launch of the programme itself coincided with the start of the re-rating from the April low of 113.5p. Capital return is the one line this stock has consistently paid up for.
evidence.why_not_priced: The RNS itself is public, so the fact is not hidden -- what is unpriced is the conjunction, which needs a domestic reader to assemble: an authority left 36% unused, terminated on a fixed date one week before results, on a company whose Board has stated in a primary document that it intends to substitute buybacks for dividends, at a point where a fresh authority would normally be announced with the interims. The programme was buying roughly GBP22k a day against GBP198k of market turnover, about a tenth of the volume in the stock, so its removal is mechanically visible in a name this thin. If the market were positioned for a relaunch there would be commentary on it; there is none from any of the five covering brokers that is publicly visible. This is the smallest and the softest of the three findings -- it rests on an inference about what the Board will do, not on a fact about what it has done -- and it is sized accordingly, with a band that crosses zero.
evidence.independence: The Board's stated intention is in a different document -- the FY25 preliminary results: 'the Board intends to reallocate the amount that would otherwise have been proposed as a final dividend for the year ended 31 December 2025' to the buyback, with statutory dividends already at nil (2024: 1.95p) -- https://www.mcsaatchiplc.com/~/media/Files/M/mc-saatchi/documents/result-centre/2025/fy-2025-results-announcement.pdf

evidence.text: Petco's Q2 and FY2026 guidance explicitly assumes NO further IEEPA tariff refunds beyond the partial one received in May 2026, yet CBP's CAPE Phase 2 opened 29 June 2026 and BARK - a pet-products importer - booked a reconciliation line item literally labelled 'IEEPA Tariffs Phase II' worth $7.363M in the quarter ended 30 June 2026, which sits entirely inside Petco's 3 May - 1 Aug fiscal Q2.
evidence.why_not_priced: The sweep found a single $0.03 EPS estimate on this name - there is no sell-side machine tracking which CAPE phase disbursed when, and no WOOF note or wire item connects BARK's 6 August Phase-II disclosure to Petco's quarter. If it were priced, WOOF would not have fallen 6.9% in the week Evercore raised its target to $4 from $3.50 (31 Aug), and the June-3 sentence 'no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year' would be quoted in previews as an explicit upside option rather than ignored. Petco's CFO quantified the direct exposure at ~7% of total merchandise COGS sourced from China/Canada/Mexico for owned brands, i.e. roughly $200M of annual import cost, so the residual refund is plausibly high-single to low-double-digit millions against a $110-112M Q2 adjusted EBITDA guide. Risk to the finding: BARK excluded its refund from adjusted EBITDA, and Petco could do the same or book it in Q3 - hence the wide band.
evidence.independence: Petco's own June-3 release states the exclusion verbatim ('our outlook assumes the benefit of a partial IEEPA tariff refund received in May 2026, with no additional refunds assumed for the balance of the year') - https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/petco-reports-first-quarter-2026-results-302790636.html (2026-06-03); the CAPE Phase 2 / Phase 3 timeline and the $40bn+ disbursed by end-June is independently documented at https://www.thompsonhinesmartrade.com/2026/06/cbp-announces-phases-2-and-3-of-the-ieepa-tariff-refund-process/ and https://www.hklaw.com/en/insights/publications/2026/06/ieepa-tariff-refund-update-government-appeals (2026-06-15); the 7% exposure figure is from CFO Sabrina Simmons via https://www.retaildive.com/news/petco-reaffirms-guidance-sales-fall-q1-tariffs/750114 (2025-06-09). NOTE: this finding and finding 2 both bear on the same June-3 Petco guidance paragraph, but the external evidence is entirely separate (CBP/BARK vs EIA/BTS diesel) - collapse the Petco release, not the two findings.

evidence.text: Petco's FY2026 guide is pinned to 'fuel prices remain elevated at approximately those experienced in the first quarter' - fiscal Q1 (Feb-Apr) averaged about $4.71/gal diesel on BTS monthlies ($3.72 / $4.92 / $5.50), fiscal Q2 (May-Jul) averaged about $5.20, and diesel was $5.599/gal on 31 Aug with US diesel cracks setting an all-time record above $106/bbl on 1 Sep and record-low seasonal distillate stocks going into heating season - leaving the stated H2 assumption roughly 19% below spot.
evidence.why_not_priced: Petco names fuel as one of only two quantified guidance assumptions, so it is material enough to move the FY $415-430M adjusted EBITDA range, yet no WOOF-specific coverage carries a diesel number. If the market had done this arithmetic the stock would not be trading with two Buy-side target actions in the last two weeks and no preview flagging the assumption as stale; the run-up of -10.5% over 20 days is too small and too undifferentiated to be this. Fiscal Q2 fuel was already inside the Q2 guide (management said the May refund would be 'approximately offset by incremental tariffs and higher fuel costs'), so the live risk is the H2/FY guide, not the Q2 print - which is why the band is wide and the upper bound is only mildly positive.
evidence.independence: Monthly BTS diesel prints corroborate the level series independently of EIA weeklies: March $4.92 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-march-2026-0), April $5.50 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-april-2026-0), May $5.60 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-may-2026-0), July $4.96 (https://www.bts.gov/newsroom/motor-fuel-prices-july-2026-0). evidence.text: The FY2025 20-F contingencies note (Note 22) says the H2-2025 loss drivers are already accrued: the Coleman/Champion judgment ($33.03M plus $1.85M in fees, under appeal since 2026-02-10 with a ruling expected in 12-18 months) and the critical-circumstances retroactive anti-dumping exposure ($6.93M plus interest). It also shows the NGCL loan guarantee fully settled on 2026-01-09 and about $28M of pledged deposits released in Feb-Mar 2026. So H1 2026 should not carry a repeat of the roughly $59M of H2-2025 charges (the $43.1M other loss plus $15.8M of impairments).
evidence.source_date: 2026-04-28 (20-F for FY2025, filed alongside the FY2025 release https://www.globenewswire.com/news-release/2026/04/28/3282414/0/en/kandi-technologies-reports-full-year-2025-financial-results.html)
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Two confirmed releases only. The H1 2025 print, which showed net income of $1.7M on revenue down 39%, reacted +13.29% (baseline). The FY2025 print, carrying the $95.6M loss that includes these charges, rose about +2.5% after the call (https://www.investing.com/news/transcripts/earnings-call-transcript-kandi-technologies-sees-247-stock-rise-post-q4-2026-call-93CH-4641460). So this holder base has already looked through these charges once.
evidence.why_not_priced: Nobody covers the name, and the note sits deep in the XBRL of a 20-F that the wire release does not reproduce: the release mentions 'anti-dumping duty expenses and increased litigation costs' with no amounts and nothing about accrual status. If the market had priced a clean H1, the stock would not be sitting at $49.6M of market cap against $211.9M of cash, restricted cash and CDs (about $113M net of short-term loans, notes payable and accrued liabilities). Most of that discount is plausibly the China-cash and governance discount, though, which this finding does not touch. Hence the small size.
evidence.independence: Partial support from a different source: management said on the 2026-04-28 call that Q1 2026 core business 'remained stable', with better per-dealer sales (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/kandi-technologies-group-q4-earnings-152903704.html). That supports the absence of new deterioration, not the absence of charges.

evidence.text: Nasdaq minimum bid-price deficiency: the compliance period ends 2026-11-02 and the stock is at $0.60. A reverse split, or a transfer to the Capital Market for another 180 days, is likely. A reverse split in a microcap is usually sold, but the decision falls after the exit window unless it is announced with the results.

The appeal of the $33M Coleman judgment in the Texas 5th Court of Appeals was filed 2026-02-10, and the company expects a ruling in 12-18 months. A reversal would release an accrued liability of about $35M, roughly 70% of market cap.

2026 6-Ks: only three, the Nasdaq notice (05-08), a director appointment (06-04) and the Xinchu 51% acquisition for RMB20M (06-29). No buyback, divestment or financing (https://www.sec.gov/cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany&CIK=0001720250&type=6-K&dateb=&owner=include&count=40)
Share buyback: the last programme was $30M in Nov 2023, and nothing has been announced in 2025-2026 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/kandi-technologies-announces-share-buyback-130000141.html)
Insider filings: Form 3s on 2026-08-28 and 09-02 look like the new FPI Section 16 regime. No Form 4 buying or selling cluster found (https://www.stocktitan.net/sec-filings/KNDI/)

IEEPA tariff refund: SCOTUS struck the tariffs down 2026-02-20 and CBP's CAPE refunds are running, but Kandi has disclosed no refund claim or receivable, so there is no company-level number (https://www.skadden.com/insights/publications/2026/03/tariff-refund-mechanism-takes-shape)

EAPA golf-cart evasion cases 8247/8282/8286 (Apr-Aug 2026) name competitor importers (ICON, Denago, Bintelli, Atlas and others) but not Kandi/SC Autosports. Possible competitive relief, but it is only a macro-to-company hypothesis and was dropped (https://www.cbp.gov/document/publications/eapa-cons-case-8286-various-importers-notice-initiation-investigation-and)
Battery-swap revenue: the CATL/Qiji 18-station order and the Lin'an production start are both July 2026, after H1, so they do not land in the reported half (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/KNDI/)
